name: Sierra Nevada Pale Ale
description: An attributed adaptation of the brewery’s published homebrew recipe, with its grain ratios and Cascade addition schedule retained.
notes: Source specifies 92% two-row and 8% caramel 60L rather than a total grain weight; this adaptation assumes 4.5 kg total and 72% efficiency. The source’s 5 US gallon batch is represented as post-boil kettle volume, with zero transfer loss for this template. Uses catalog Briess malts and WLP001 for the source’s generic two-row, caramel and California ale yeast. Cascade weights and 90/60/30/0-minute timings follow the source; the zero-minute addition is flameout, with no assumed hop-stand duration. Source calls for whole cones; this engine has no pellet/cone adjustment. A 170°F (76.7°C), 5-minute mash-out is written here for manual use because the model stores one mash rest. Boil-off, carbonation and pitch settings are app assumptions. Calculated values are this app’s predictions, not the brewery’s specifications.

name: Sierra Nevada Torpedo Extra IPA
description: A catalog adaptation of Sierra Nevada’s published Torpedo homebrew recipe, retaining its malt weights and hop schedule.
notes: Uses the source’s 13.25 lb pale malt, 1 lb caramel 60L, 70/10/0-minute kettle additions and dry-hop masses. WLP001 maps its generic California ale yeast. Whole-cone/pellet differences are not modeled. Source mash is 155°F for 90 min; a 170°F, 5-min mash-out remains a manual step. Zero-minute additions are flameout without an invented hop stand. Source places dry hopping after 1–2 days of primary; the app’s 3-day contact is an assumption because contact duration is not given. The 5-gallon yield is represented as post-boil volume with zero transfer loss; 72% efficiency, boil-off and carbonation are app settings. Source finishing criterion is 3.7°P; the engine’s attenuation prediction is independent.

name: Bell’s Two Hearted IPA
description: A published Two Hearted clone by Bell’s General Store staff, adapted to the app’s ingredient catalog.
notes: Published by the Homebrewers Association and credited to David Curtis and Ryan Kramer of Bell’s General Store. Retains 10 lb two-row, 2.83 lb pale ale malt, 8 oz caramel 40L and the 34/34/99 g Centennial schedule at 9.1% AA. Uses published 65% efficiency, 19 L and 75-min boil. Represents the initial mash as 150°F for 45 min; the ramp and 170°F rest remain manual. Source gypsum addition and conditioning stages are not modeled. Source chills to 64°F; this is the single fermentation set point used here, rather than a complete temperature schedule. Source suggests dry hopping a week into fermentation for a week. Whirlpool settling is not a whirlpool hop dose.

name: Sierra Nevada Celebration Ale
description: A published Celebration Ale homebrew interpretation, using its all-grain version rather than mixing in the extract alternative.
notes: Published source lists 10 lb two-row, 1.5 lb crystal 25–40L, 0.5 lb dextrin malt, and the stated hop masses/AA. Maps the crystal to catalog caramel 40L and dextrin to Briess Carapils. Mash 154°F for 60 min uses the longer end of the source’s 45–60 min range. The 90-min boil follows the earliest hop time. Whirlpool contact time is unspecified and represented as zero rather than inventing utilization; set your own stand time. Three-day dry-hop contact, 72% efficiency, boil-off and carbonation are app assumptions. Fermentation 68°F is carried from the source’s process discussion. Source figures are displayed separately from recalculated predictions.

name: Stone Ruination IPA

notes: Official reference lists Magnum, Chinook and Centennial, 8.2% ABV and 100+ IBU. This house recipe chooses the grain bill, sugar, proportions, timing and yeast. High-IBU prediction and perceived bitterness are especially uncertain.
